transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-23 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Redwood CSM), Dr. Sara Goldstein (CISO - Helios), Tom Alvarez (Head of Platform), Emily Park (Legal), Ian Wu (Infra)

Summary (auto): Security posture discovery for Helios Diagnostics evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: PHI/PII handling, key management, auditability, SSO integration, data residency/retention and legal requirements.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call - Alex from Redwood AE here, Priya our SE, Jordan CSM. Sara, Tom, Emily, Ian on the Helios side?
[00:08] Dr. Sara: Yep, Sara here, hi.
[00:10] Tom: Tom here.
[00:12] Emily: Emily.
[00:13] Ian: Ian.
[00:15] Alex: Great, so objective today is to understand your security posture and see which deployment model makes sense - hosted, dedicated, or private. Priya will jump into some technical detail.
[00:25] Priya: Hi all, quick context - Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC/on-prem. For PHI workloads people often look at Private for full network control and KMS integration, but Dedicated with customer-managed keys is a middle ground. Just call out up front, I'll use some shorthand and sorry if I mangle any of your internal names.
[00:44] Dr. Sara: Perfect. Our primary requirement is that no PHI leaves our control unencrypted, and audit trails for every call. We want to understand your SOC2 and ISO posture and also how SSO/SAML integrates with RBAC.
[00:56] Alex: Totally. We're SOC2 Type II and have ISO 27001 in progress/up to date - we'll share the artifacts after this call. In Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit, we also have a KMS integration for Dedicated and Private where you keep the keys.
[01:10] Emily: When you say KMS integration for Dedicated, do you mean Redwood uses our KMS or you can accept customer-managed keys? Legal needs to understand who actually has the key material.
[01:18] Priya: For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS - we can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via standard key wrap. Redwood doesn't persist plaintext key material; keys are used to encrypt model cache and logs where applicable. For Hosted we manage keys by default but we do offer bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise contracts.
[01:41] Ian: Is that HSM-backed? We have a compliance note requiring HSM for certain environments.
[01:45] Priya: Yes, we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS or cloud KMS backed by HSM. We'll include technical integration notes.
[01:52] Tom: Audit logs - we need per-call auditability, with request/response hashes, user identities, and timestamps. How fine-grained are your logs and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[02:03] Priya: We emit structured audit events with request metadata, route/model, token usage, and identity. For Private we can forward logs directly into your logging pipeline or S3 bucket. For Hosted we offer log exporting via secure transfer, and for Dedicated we can set up streaming to your SIEM.
[02:18] Dr. Sara: Data retention policy - we need to ensure short retention for PII and the ability to purge. How does Redwood handle retention and data deletion requests?
[02:26] Alex: Good question. By default Hosted retains request payloads for 30 days for debugging and training isolation, but we can change retention windows per contract and offer options to disable retention for certain routes. Dedicated/Private give you control to set retention to near-zero and we can configure auto-purge. We'll provide the retention policy doc.
[02:45] Emily: Is there guaranteed deletion? We need evidence for audits.
[02:49] Priya: We have documented deletion workflows and can provide attestation and logs for deletion events. For Private, deletion is performed within your environment depending on how you configure S3 and object lifecycle.
[03:01] Tom: SSO/SAML and RBAC - we use Okta and expect SAML-based SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Also want fine-grained role mapping for who can create routes, change rollouts, and read logs.
[03:12] Priya: We integrate with SAML/SSO providers including Okta, Azure AD. SCIM is supported for user provisioning. RBAC supports roles like Admin, Dev, Viewer, and custom role mapping. We can map SAML attributes into RBAC groups.
[03:26] Ian: Any MFA enforcement hooks? We have a conditional access policy.
[03:30] Alex: We rely on your IdP for MFA enforcement - Redwood respects the SAML assertion; for console/API access we support short-lived tokens and can enforce session timeouts.
[03:40] Dr. Sara: For Private deployments, network controls are a big deal. Can you outline the networking options? VPC peering, private link, on-prem appliance?
[03:50] Priya: Options include VPC peering, PrivateLink (cloud provider dependent), and an on-prem package for air-gapped or restricted environments. We can put the control plane in your VPC or use a hybrid approach. We'll share our private deployment network diagram.
[04:05] Tom: Performance tradeoffs - if we run Private with HSM and strict network egress controls, what's the latency impact? We need sub-200ms tail latency for short prompt paths.
[04:16] Priya: There is some overhead for network hops and key unwraps, but with Dedicated and Private optimizations we generally hit sub-200ms for small generations with warm KV cache and batching tuned. For strict HSM operations we can cache decrypted keys in a transient secure enclave to reduce latency. We'll propose a benchmark configuration.
[04:36] Dr. Sara: Do you offer model variant fallback for high availability? If we're pinned to a large model and capacity is constrained, can you autoswitch to a compatible quantized variant without leaking data?
[04:48] Priya: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants and we maintain isolation semantics. Fallbacks are configurable and we can ensure logs/audit indicate fallback events for compliance.
[05:00] Emily: Contracts and legal - we need to review your data processing addendum and standard IP terms. Also liability caps around PHI exposures.
[05:09] Alex: We'll send standard DPA and our enterprise contract template; for PHI-specific clauses we can coordinate with your legal team. Jordan will follow up.
[05:18] Jordan: I'll own the NDA/contract follow up.
[05:22] Tom: Encryption in transit - TLS ciphers, mutual TLS for private endpoints?
[05:26] Priya: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and can do mTLS for Private endpoints. Cipher suites follow industry best practices, and we'll list them in the security whitepaper.
[05:36] Ian: How about model telemetry? We need to make sure no raw responses containing PII are sent to external telemetry or training datasets.
[05:44] Priya: Redwood has an opt-out for telemetry and we do not use customer request/response content for training without explicit permission. For Hosted we have a default opt-in for anonymous telemetry; enterprise customers can disable that.
[05:58] Dr. Sara: Can you provide evidence for SOC2 controls around change management and vulnerability scanning?
[06:05] Alex: Yes, we have control mappings, vulnerability scan reports, and change logs. We'll share a SOC2 summary and control mapping doc.
[06:14] Emily: Data residency - our data must remain in the US. Does Redwood support regional isolation for Hosted?
[06:21] Priya: Hosted can be regionally isolated (US-only), but Dedicated and Private give you more deterministic residency. We'll call out regions where we operate.
[06:32] Tom: For the pilot, what minimal scope would show us compliance and performance?
[06:36] Priya: We recommend a short smoke test: 1) connect SSO and provisioning, 2) run 72-hour request stream with synthetic PII masked prompts, 3) confirm logs/forwarding and KMS flows, 4) run simple latency/throughput tests for common endpoints. We can do that in a Dedicated or Private staging account.
[07:00] Dr. Sara: Cost - we need a sense of Dedicated reserved capacity pricing and the uplift for HSM/backups.
[07:07] Alex: We'll provide a pricing sheet with Dedicated commit options and premium add-ons (HSM, extended retention, increased observability retention).
[07:14] Emily: Legal will need data processing terms before any production pilot.
[07:18] Jordan: I'll attach the DPA and schedule a legal-to-legal review.
[07:23] Tom: Is there a way to redact or mask PII automatically at the proxy layer before it hits the model?
[07:29] Priya: We offer optional middleware for deterministic PII masking and routing rules; also customers build pre-processing to strip/replace entities. We'll share our masking best-practices doc.
[07:41] Alex: Any other blockers or stakeholders to bring in for next meeting?
[07:45] Dr. Sara: I'd like our external audit manager on the next call and possibly one of our privacy leads. Also, legal to send NDA redlines.
[07:55] Emily: We'll review the SOC2 artifact when you send it.
[07:58] Alex: Okay great. Recap and next steps - we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, private deployment network diagram, KMS/HSM integration note, pricing and pilot proposal, DPA template. Priya will prepare a sizing and benchmark plan.
[08:15] Dr. Sara: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:18] Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up by Thursday with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
